summary: Redwood AE+SE provided a console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer (DataWave Labs) is evaluating Redwood for inference serving for a recommendation product. Key concerns: latency SLOs, data residency, audit logs, KMS integration. Agreed next steps: share security artifacts, run benchmark with sample workload, and scope a 4-week pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from Redwood, with priya on the line, we'll do a 45-ish minute walkthrough of the console focusing on tracing, error analysis and request logs, and leave time for q&a.
[00:12] Marta Lopez: thanks, alex. we have about 45 minutes, james and ethan are here from platform and security. our primary goal today is to understand how we'd debug production inference issues and get the audit logs we need.
[00:28] Priya Nair: cool, i'll share my screen now. bear with me if the layout looks a bit different, i'm on the staging console. (screen share) 
[00:40] Priya Nair: okay, so this is the redwood console landing page, quick nav 

models, routes, requests, tracing. i'm going to jump to tracing. note: some of the auto labels are off in staging, you might see "redood" instead of "redwood" in a couple places, apologies.
[01:05] James Reed: ha, no worries. first question 

can you show how traces map to request ids? we want to correlate high latency requests to user events in our system.
[01:18] Priya Nair: yes, great question. in the requests view each request has a request_id and a link to the trace. here's an example: request 8f3a2d 

click into it, we show a waterfall of spans: client->proxy->executor, kv-cache hits, kernel time. the trace includes timing for tokenization, model compute and post-processing.
[01:40] Priya Nair: (typing) and you can filter traces by latency > 200ms, or by error status, or by model shard.
[01:50] Marta Lopez: does the tracing include the kv cache metrics? sometimes we see cache thrash in our workloads.
[01:56] Priya Nair: yes, we instrument kv cache events. you'll see cache_hit/miss spans and we annotate with key sizes and approximate idx. in addition, the console surface shows hit rate over time for the selected route.
[02:12] Ethan Kim: what about PII? traces 

do they ever contain request payloads or user tokens? that's a security concern for us.
[02:20] Alex Chen: good callout 

by default traces do not store raw prompt text in the UI; we store hashes and metadata. raw payload capture is an opt-in for debugging and is gated behind RBAC + audit logs, and behind KMS encryption. sum: we can enable raw capture for a limited window for the pilot but it's auditable.
[02:42] James Reed: so the raw payload is encrypted with customer KMS? we use Azure Key Vault for keys.
[02:48] Priya Nair: yep, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). we can integrate with Azure KV or AWS KMS; the raw data at rest for traces is encrypted with the CMK. and we log key usage in the audit trail.
[03:05] Marta Lopez: okay great. can you demo an error case end-to-end? we had a recent incident where a subset of requests returned malformed json from the model and we couldn't reproduce.
[03:16] Priya Nair: absolutely. let me search in requests for status = 500 and body contains "parse error". (search) here's a cluster of failures around 10:42am yesterday. click one.
[03:30] Priya Nair: in the request details we show the raw truncated output (if capture is enabled), model variant, tokenizer length, and the trace. the trace shows a long compute span followed by a termination event: "model-runtime exception: decode error at token 213".
[03:47] Priya Nair: also you'll notice a side panel with correlated requests 

same client, same prompt prefix 

which helps identify pattern.
[03:58] James Reed: that correlation view is helpful, can we export these slices to csv for offline analysis?
[04:04] Priya Nair: yes, exports are supported, and you can also open the request set in the optimize tab to run diff-evals or batch reruns. we'll share a sample workbook link after the call.
[04:18] Marta Lopez: you mentioned model variants 

how do rollbacks work when we push a new model and see regressions?
[04:26] Alex Chen: rollouts are controlled per route. you can do canary traffic split, automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval sets, or manual rollback. the console exposes the rollout history and the step that triggered an automatic fallback.
[04:42] Sofia Tran: what's the latency overhead of tracing? we can't add too much tail latency.
[04:50] Priya Nair: tracing is asynchronous by default; we sample at route level. full capture does add overhead but we recommend sampling 1-5% for production and 100% for short debugging windows. the runtime attaches minimal in-process spans 

most heavy lifting is done by the telemetry pipeline.
[05:09] James Reed: do you support distributed tracing integrations like Jaeger or OpenTelemetry exports?
[05:15] Priya Nair: yes we export to OTLP/Jaeger and you can map our spans into your existing trace id. we also support ingesting an upstream trace id from your proxy so you can connect frontend->redwood traces.
[05:30] Marta Lopez: can we configure retention windows for request logs and traces? some of our regs require 12 months of certain audit logs.
[05:38] Alex Chen: retention is configurable; default is 90 days for full request logs, and you can opt into longer archival tiers (S3 or GCS export) for up to 12 months+ with additional fees. audit logs are separate 

we maintain immutable audit trails that can be streamed to your SIEM.
[05:55] Ethan Kim: speaking of audit, show me where the audit logs live and what they contain.
[06:02] Priya Nair: sure. the audit view shows admin actions: role changes, KMS operations, config changes, who accessed raw captures, etc. each entry has actor, timestamp, IP, and an immutable event id. we also have a compliance package that describes retention and access controls 

alex will share that doc.
[06:20] Marta Lopez: great. please do.
[06:23] Priya Nair: switching to the error analysis page 

at the top we aggregate errors by class: model_decode, timeout, runtime-exception, quota_exceeded. clicking into model_decode shows examples, golden prompts, frequency, and a small chart of token positions where decode errors commonly happen.
[06:44] Priya Nair: you can pin a set of failing prompts and run them through previous model versions or quantization profiles to triage whether it's a model regression or an execution issue.
[06:58] James Reed: does that work with quantized backends? we run 4-bit quant on some variants and want to know if it's causing decode artifacts.
[07:06] Priya Nair: yes, the console tags the backends and quantization profile for each request. the diff tooling can re-run the prompt on a float32 variant in a sandbox to compare outputs side-by-side.
[07:20] Marta Lopez: nice. how do request logs show up for high-volume traffic 

is there sampling or indexing we should be aware of?
[07:29] Priya Nair: for high volume routes we automatically sample request payloads and keep full metadata for all requests (latency, route, model, status). you can apply route-level rules to increase capture for specific user ids or session ids. indexing supports fast queries on attributes like request_id, model, status, and custom tags.
[07:48] Alex Chen: and you can attach custom tags programmatically in the API request so your internal user id is available for filtering, obv you can hash it if you don't want PII.
[08:00] Marta Lopez: that's important for us. james, from platform's perspective any other concerns?
[08:05] James Reed: networking and VPC peering 

we need to ensure private deployment can reach our vault and that outbound IPs can be whitelisted.
[08:14] Alex Chen: for Private we support VPC peering and on-prem connectors; outbound IPs can be fixed for Dedicated as well. we'll provide a network diagram and required ACL entries.
[08:25] Ethan Kim: latency numbers 

can you show a dashboard of p99 over the last week? we care about tail.
[08:31] Priya Nair: sure, open the route dashboard 

here's p50/p95/p99 with canaries overlaid. you can also change the aggregation window and compare against cost per token. (cursor moves) you can see we surface token-level breakdowns: tokenization, kv-cache, kernel, io.
[08:53] Sofia Tran: that token-level breakdown will help us prioritize optimization.
[08:57] Marta Lopez: what about alerts and integrations? we want slack alerts when error rate crosses threshold.
[09:04] Priya Nair: alerts are rule-based and send to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook. you can alert on trace-derived metrics, e.g., sudden increase in kv miss rate.
[09:14] James Reed: back to the malformed json case 

can we set an automated reroute of a small percentage of traffic to a float32 variant if we detect increased parse errors?
[09:24] Alex Chen: yes, that's a common pattern. routing policies can be latency-first or quality-first; we support fallback to a compatible model variant automatically. you can also set it as a canary step to divert 2-5% while we monitor.
[09:38] Priya Nair: (navigating) here's the routing policy editor. you can create a rule: if error_rate > 1% for 10 minutes then split traffic to float32 variant and notify. and the UI shows the active policy and historical triggers.
[09:55] Marta Lopez: nice. our security team will ask about data residency 

we need EU-only storage for certain customers.
[10:03] Alex Chen: we have region controls; logs and traces can be stored in-region. for Private deployments we can keep everything in your VPC. for Hosted we support EU regions with at-rest separation.
[10:16] Ethan Kim: can we get a sample retention policy config?
[10:19] Alex Chen: yes, i'll attach the policy templates in a follow-up.
[10:22] Priya Nair: moving on 

request logs UI. this is the live stream of incoming requests. you can apply filters and save them as saved-views. each row includes request_id, status, latency, model, route, user_tag. clicking expands details and links to trace and any stored output.
[10:44] Priya Nair: one handy feature is the replay button 

it will replay the request through a sandboxed runner against a specified variant. it's safe and doesn't affect production state.
[10:56] James Reed: replay sounds useful; is it rate-limited or auditable?
[11:01] Priya Nair: it's auditable in the audit log, and we rate-limit replays per account to avoid accidental load. you can also queue replays to run as a batch.
[11:12] Marta Lopez: if we replay against older model versions can we compare token-by-token and get a metric for regression?
[11:20] Priya Nair: yes, the diff tool shows token diffs, log-prob deltas, and a simple quality score based on your eval rubric. you can add prompts to a regression suite.
[11:33] Sofia Tran: what about integrations with our monitoring stack? we use Datadog.
[11:37] Priya Nair: we have native Datadog metrics and logs export, plus OTLP for traces. we can push request-level metrics and aggregate counts.
[11:47] Alex Chen: quick note on cost 

the console surfaces per-route cost estimates, and when you rerun prompts in optimize, you see projected cost and a delta if you switch to quantized variants.
[12:00] James Reed: can we get an exported cost report for a given date range?
[12:04] Priya Nair: yep, billing exports are available and you can map them to routes or project tags.
[12:12] Marta Lopez: i'd like to understand the POC scope 

priya, what would you need to run the benchmark you mentioned?
[12:19] Priya Nair: ideally: a sample corpus of 2k representative prompts, a traffic profile (rps distribution, token lengths), a set of success metrics (latency p95 target, quality metric threshold). access: a test API key and optional vault access for KMS. we'll run the job on a dedicated pool and share results and a runbook.
[12:40] James Reed: security will want the test data in a sanitized form. we'll provide hashed ids.
[12:45] Ethan Kim: also want to confirm network steps for peering.
[12:48] Alex Chen: james, i'll send the network diagram and a short checklist.
[12:52] Marta Lopez: turning back to error analysis 

can alerts auto-open a ticket in our ticketing system? we use Jira.
[12:59] Priya Nair: yes, webhooks can create Jira issues or trigger automation; you can customize payloads.
[13:07] Sofia Tran: one more question 

how do we surface false positives for errors caused by prompt templating in our side?
[13:13] Priya Nair: the console has a prompt-variant clustering view that groups similar prefixes. you can tag clusters as "client-side templating" and exclude them from alerting rules.
[13:26] James Reed: what about role-based access 

can we limit who can view raw captures and who can trigger replays?
[13:33] Alex Chen: yes, RBAC is granular. roles include: viewer, operator, auditor, admin. raw capture permission is a separate flag and any access is written to the audit log with reason.
[13:46] Ethan Kim: will the audit log show the decrypted content access events or just the fact that a user requested it?
[13:52] Priya Nair: it records the access event and a pointer to the capture id; decrypt operations are also logged (actor and KMS key used). we don't store decrypted content in the audit log.
[14:05] Marta Lopez: good.
[14:07] Priya Nair: quick demo of a replay: selecting a failed request, hitting replay, choosing float32 variant, queued, and the diff shows extra tokens truncated 

looks like decode error due to tokenizer mismatch in a quant profile.
[14:25] Sofia Tran: any way to automatically create a regression ticket with sample failing prompts and stack trace?
[14:31] Priya Nair: yes, there's a "Create Bug" workflow that packages the sample, trace link, config and rerun artifact. it can populate Jira fields.
[14:44] James Reed: ok that's useful. next question: our compliance team asks about SOC2 and pen test cadence.
[14:50] Alex Chen: we are SOC2 Type II and do annual penetration tests. we'll share the attestation and a summary of the pen test scope. also we publish our incident response runbook.
[15:05] Ethan Kim: fine. can you include the exact checklist for onboarding for private/dedicated? we need to budget time.
[15:12] Alex Chen: onboarding checklist: network setup (VPC peering or transit), KMS integration, SSO (SAML/SCIM), role mappings, sample traffic and security review. for Dedicated typical timeline is 4-6 weeks, Private (on-prem) longer depending on infra.
[15:30] Marta Lopez: timeline aligns with ours.
[15:33] Priya Nair: last section 

debugging playbook. we have a template with steps: reproduce in sandbox, check request logs, pull trace, run replay, if persistent escalate to runtime team with runbook attachment. i'll attach that.
[15:49] Marta Lopez: excellent. any limitations we should know?
[15:53] Priya Nair: a few: archived long-term raw captures are slower to access (cold tier), sampling means not every request has a full trace unless you enable capture, and in extremely high throughput scenarios very fine-grained token-level metrics may be approximate. we'll document these in the runbook.
[16:12] James Reed: are there quotas we need to be aware of for replays or debug runs?
[16:17] Alex Chen: replays are metered 

small allowances in pilot, and then you can purchase debug credits for heavier usage.
[16:26] Ethan Kim: what's the SLA for log ingestion and trace availability? we need to know if a recent outage will impact our forensic abilities.
[16:33] Priya Nair: logs/trace ingestion SLA is 99.9% for Dedicated with the premium telemetry retention, and for Hosted it's part of our standard SLA 

we can put the exact numbers in the security pack.
[16:45] Marta Lopez: ok. wrapping up, we probably want the pilot to include: 2k prompts, 1 week of simulated traffic, enable 1% full capture for targeted routes, replay and diff tooling access.
[16:59] Alex Chen: sounds good 

we'll scope that and include acceptance criteria: p95 < 200ms, error rate < 0.5%, quality threshold X (to be defined by marta).
[17:12] James Reed: timeline 

can we start the bench week of 10/27?
[17:16] Priya Nair: yes, we'll aim for that, pending sample data and network checklist.
[17:21] Marta Lopez: great, we'll get the data and confirm by 10/22.
[17:25] Sofia Tran: thanks everyone

quick last q: will you share the console recording or deck?
[17:29] Alex Chen: yes i'll share the recording and priya will share the runbook and example queries.
[17:34] (brief crosstalk)
[17:40] Alex Chen: okay if no further q's let's recap next steps 

alex send security docs and network diagram, priya run benchmark and set up replay job, james provide sample traffic and ACLs.
[17:53] Marta Lopez: sounds good. thanks all.
[18:00] Priya Nair: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links. bye.
[54:30] (call end)
